text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The government will probably decide on next year's anti-inflation measures in three weeks, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told Reuters.
- Only two MPs had so far chosen to give up their seats in favour of outside business interests to comply with the conflict of interests law.

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told Monday to a Socialist Party faction that "as long as I am prime minister, I will not support any changes or turnabout in the policies pursued by the government and the Socialist Party."
- Socialist MPs rejected a plan to look into properties of the former Communist Party and probe the properties of the Young Democrats and the Democratic Forum.
- The amount devoted to agriculture will be increased in line with GDP growth in real terms, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said.
- If Hungary buys fighter planes made under a British-Swedish agreement, Swedish businessmen will invest substantial sums in Hungary.
- Parliament began the debate of a bill on auditing and a proposed Hungarian Chamber of Auditors.
- First quarter net household savings came to Ft 122.5 billion, below the Ft 133.5 billion registered in January-March 1996.
- The third and last group of companies to be sold off through simplified privatization includes 19 firms, State Privatization & Holding Co. (APV Rt.) said.
- Workers at the meat factory Szekszard Husipari Rt. continued their strike Monday, demanding that an 18% salary increase be made retroactive to January.
- The lucky winner who hits the five correct numbers will win Ft 582 million this week, the biggest win in the history of the Hungarian lottery since it was established in 1957.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Armed Forces Chief of Staff Ferenc Vegh said Monday that 1.5% of GDP, as against this year's 1.2%, is needed to finance low-scale development of the Hungarian military.
- The Finance Ministry denied charges by the farmers' group Metesz that the government went back on its earlier promises to them.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Hungary's banking sector's aggregate 1996 after-tax profit exceeded that in the previous year by over 60% and came to Ft 68 billion.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
The MInistry of Interior has launched a tender to a value of Ft 3 billion for the purchase of police cars.
